problem.observed: The b5 iPhone passed Edit memory book readiness, then failed Page 1 after the semantic Open book tap. Its saved error image has blank cover artwork with closed-book controls; a later capture-flow error image shows the first page with the exact expected label.
problem.sourceMechanism: The authorized loaded reader was published only by the callback from Animated.timing. The cover fades to zero before that callback changes opened. A delayed, absent or interrupted completion can leave content unavailable after the user presses Open book.
problem.provenByControlledRegression: The literal b5 component fails four actual-component cases when acknowledgement is held or interrupted: iOS, Android, reduced motion, and finished:false. Its27 prior loading/reaction/authorization cases and five new lifecycle/continuity controls pass.
problem.causalityLimit: This establishes and removes the completion dependency. It does not establish why native callback delivery or capture URL delivery was late in the real run, and does not claim the next native run will pass.

change.behavior: Open book now calls setOpened(true) directly. The next committed render can expose the already-authorized reader without receiving any native animation acknowledgement.
change.scope: Only the openBook callback and its dependencies/comment change. Required auth/book/media gates, optional reaction handling, owner/route invalidation, explicit closeBook, page-turn cancellation, saved-book operations and film/export parent callbacks remain unchanged.
change.implementationReason: No clock, timeout, promise, retry, retained content overlay or new asynchronous handoff is introduced. The stable React state setter is the callback’s only dependency, so an empty useCallback dependency list is valid.

tests.boundary: The complete production MemoryAlbumScreen and pure shared helpers execute with controlled React hook scheduling, auth/transport/media responses and native primitives. The animation boundary intentionally withholds/reports completion. MemoryPageTurn and other child native components are stubs in this harness; native pixels, CoreAnimation delivery, real React concurrent scheduling and device timing are not simulated.

limits: The current b5 iPhone and Android required native flows remain failed; this local repair does not retroactively change their outcomes.
The entry regression proves component state is not gated by native completion, not a production frame-rate or end-to-end latency claim.
The capture route mounted and saved-account readback passed after the b5 heading deadline. This change does not modify or claim to solve that separate event-delivery delay.
Book/account/route invalidation remains in the existing component and parent lifecycle; no authorization or stale-content allowance is introduced.
No Maestro selector, deadline, test order, iOS signing path, Android renderer, app capability flag or provider behavior is changed by this two-file repair.
Independent review and an actual new full-native run are still required for native acceptance.
